# 1.2.31 - the curtain as it was, and the wall measured

1.2.30 broke the curtain in two ways that were visible at the table, and one
that probably was. All three are undone or fixed here; everything else in
1.2.30 stands.

**The blocks stand at their angle again.** 1.2.30 stood every block straight
on any screen under 2200 px wide, which is every tablet. That was a rule where
the audit had offered a choice, and the tilt was the look. It is back to
6-8 degrees everywhere, exactly as in 1.2.27.

**The wall is measured, not assumed.** 1.2.30 asked Foundry whether the
sidebar was expanded through a property it could not verify existed, and
treated an unanswered question as "yes" - so the glass kept a wall against
the collapsed tab rail, some fifty pixels short of the screen's edge, and
collapsing the sidebar never restored the glass. Foundry's answer is used
only when it is actually a boolean; otherwise the part of the sidebar that
collapses is measured, and a rail is never a wall. `drpgGlassDebug()` now
prints every reading the decision rests on.

**No wobble on a recut.** Measuring the blocks turns their rotation off for
one style pass, and the blocks carry an 840 ms transition on `transform` -
so every recut swung every block from 0 degrees back to its tilt. 1.2.30
recuts far more often than 1.2.27 did (that was the point of it), which made
the swing constant. Transitions are held still for the length of the pass.

The Event panel also gains its ticker and the card for a body being found,
the ballot is a list of names rather than a drop-down, and the three dots
under the clock's room line - the room's search tokens - take the theme's
shape and colour.
